sentences.text: On 25 November Uranus is at opposition: Sun, Earth and Uranus line up, and the planet stays in the sky all night.
Opposition is the moment an outer planet is closest to Earth and at its brightest; Uranus is now two point six billion kilometres from us.
Seen from Earth it sits in Aries, a blue-green point at magnitude five point six, barely visible to the naked eye under a dark sky and easy in binoculars.
Its colour comes from methane in its atmosphere absorbing red light.
With its axis tipped on its side, Uranus all but rolls along its eighty-four-year journey around the Sun.
